quotes.text: We want to make certain that we continue with school choice because that provides parents options.
quotes.editor_note: From a WVLT sit-down interview alongside her two primary opponents (2026-07-23) on school choice; Blackburn pledges to keep and grow Tennessee's Education Freedom Scholarship voucher program, the opposite of Fritts's cancel-the-program stance in the same interview. Verbatim, no edits.

quotes.text: We have some of our state leaders who want to do a Tennessee DOGE. I support that. Let's take that big red marker to programs that have outlived their usefulness.
quotes.editor_note: From a WKRN interview on affordability (WKRN's own page blocks automated fetches; text confirmed via a syndicated Yahoo News copy, wording is the publisher's direct quotation) where Blackburn was asked about cutting the grocery tax; she answers with a spending-review-first approach — cut programs before cutting taxes — a leaner-government stance on the tax-vs-spending tradeoff.

quotes.text: Let's make certain our communities are safe, our schools are safe, let's pick up the pace deporting illegal aliens.
quotes.editor_note: From the same WVLT sit-down interview, on how aggressively the state should pursue deportation; Blackburn ties faster deportation directly to community and school safety, an enforcement-first stance. Verbatim, no edits.

quotes.text: We must reduce the barriers to developing and building homes, which means limited and simplified permitting.
quotes.editor_note: From Blackburn's written answer to the Nashville Banner's July 2026 candidate questionnaire on housing affordability — a campaign written statement (text, not video-verifiable), flagged here as a lower-tier source. Her fix is supply-side deregulation (simpler permitting), not public intervention. Verbatim, no edits.
